text: Every chat-based LLM API organizes a conversation around three roles. The content is the same everywhere — standing instructions, what the human said, what the model said — but where those roles actually live in the request is where providers genuinely diverge, and it's a real source of bugs when you port code between them.

System holds standing instructions that apply to the whole conversation, once — persona, tone, formatting rules. User is what the human said. Assistant is what the model said, including replies you supply yourself just to seed conversation history. Simple split. The complexity is all in where they live.

In Anthropic's Messages API, system is its own top-level field, completely separate from the messages array. And messages itself only ever holds two roles: user and assistant. System never appears inside that array — it's set once, outside it, and applies to every turn that follows.

OpenAI does it differently. System lives inside the messages array as just another role, right alongside user and assistant. Same underlying idea — standing instructions, then alternating turns — but a different shape. Port code between the two without noticing this, and your system prompt either silently vanishes or the request gets rejected.

One more rule worth memorizing for Anthropic specifically: the messages array always starts on a user message, and turns alternate strictly — user, assistant, user, assistant. The documentation is explicit that consecutive same-role messages get merged into a single turn rather than erroring, which is an easy bug to miss. And there's no server-side session here — you resend the entire conversation history on every single call.

Three roles, two different ways to arrange them, and one alternation rule to not forget. Next lesson moves from who's talking to how they sound — temperature and the other sampling parameters that control how random or how deterministic a reply actually is. See you there.
